In applied mathematics, the '''Rosenbrock system matrix''' or '''Rosenbrock's system matrix''' of a linear time-invariant system is a useful representation bridging [[state space representation|state-space representation]] and [[transfer function matrix]] form. It was proposed in 1967 by [[Howard Harry Rosenbrock|Howard H. Rosenbrock]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Rosenbrock|first1=H. H.|title=Transformation of linear constant system equations|journal=Proc. IEE|date=1967|volume=114|pages=541–544}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Consider the dynamic system
<math display="block">\begin{align}
\dot{x} &= Ax +Bu, \\
y &= Cx +Du.
\end{align}</math>
The Rosenbrock system matrix is given by 
<math display="block">P(s) = \begin{pmatrix}
sI-A & -B\\
C  & D
\end{pmatrix}.</math>
In the original work by Rosenbrock, the constant matrix <math>D</math> is allowed to be a polynomial in <math>s</math>.

The transfer function between the input <math>i</math>  and output <math>j</math> is given by 
<math display="block">g_{ij}=\frac{\begin{vmatrix}
sI-A & -b_i\\
c_j  & d_{ij}
\end{vmatrix}}{|sI-A|}</math>
where <math>b_i</math> is the column <math>i</math> of <math>B</math> and <math>c_j</math> is the row <math>j</math> of <math>C</math>.

Based in this representation, Rosenbrock developed his version of the [[Hautus lemma|PBH test]].

==Short form==

For computational purposes, a short form of the Rosenbrock system matrix is more appropriate<ref>{{cite book|last1=Rosenbrock|first1=H. H.|title=State-Space and Multivariable Theory|date=1970|publisher=Nelson}}</ref> and given by
<math display="block">P\sim\begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ C & D \end{pmatrix}.</math>
The short form of the Rosenbrock system matrix has been widely used in [[H-infinity methods in control theory]], where it is also referred to as packed form; see command '''pck''' in MATLAB.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mu Analysis and Synthesis Toolbox|url=http://radio.feld.cvut.cz/matlab/toolbox/mutools/pck.html|accessdate=25 August 2014}}</ref> An interpretation of the Rosenbrock System Matrix as a Linear Fractional Transformation can be found in.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Zhou|first1=Kemin|last2=Doyle|first2=John C.|last3=Glover|first3=Keith|title=Robust and Optimal Control|date=1995|publisher=Prentice Hall}}</ref>

One of the first applications of the Rosenbrock form was the development of an efficient computational method for [[Kalman decomposition]], which is based on the pivot element method. A variant of Rosenbrock’s method is implemented in the '''minreal''' command of Matlab<ref>{{cite journal|last1=De Schutter|first1=B.|title=Minimal state-space realization in linear system theory: an overview|journal=Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics|date=2000|volume=121|issue=1–2|pages=331–354|doi=10.1016/S0377-0427(00)00341-1|bibcode=2000JCoAM.121..331S |doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[GNU Octave]].
